headerDisplay:
Publishes Enphase Envoy / IQ Gateway solar production and home consumption as **Matter electrical sensors**, so they appear in the Apple Home Energy view on iOS 27 and later.

This plugin registers no HomeKit accessories. It requires **Homebridge 2.4.0 or later** with **Matter enabled on this plugin's child bridge** (Bridge Settings -> enable Matter).

It installs alongside `homebridge-enphase-envoy` and does not replace it — the two use separate plugin names, platform blocks and child bridges.

name.title: Name
name.description: Name for this gateway. Used as the prefix for the published sensor names.

host.title: Address
host.description: Hostname or IP address of the gateway. Defaults to envoy.local.

envoyFirmware7xxTokenGenerationMode.title: Authentication

oneOf.title: Enlighten credentials - firmware v7 and later
Own token - firmware v7 and later

envoyFirmware7xxTokenGenerationMode.description: Firmware v7 and later require a JWT. Generate it from your Enlighten credentials, or paste a token you generated yourself.

envoyToken.title: Token
envoyToken.description: A JWT you generated yourself at entrez.enphaseenergy.com.

envoyPasswd.title: Envoy password
envoyPasswd.description: Only needed on firmware v5/v6 if the gateway password is not the last six digits of its serial number.

productionEnabled.title: Publish solar production
productionEnabled.description: Publish a Matter electrical sensor reporting PV production.

productionName.title: Solar production name
productionName.description: Name of the production sensor. Defaults to "<Name> Solar Production".

consumptionEnabled.title: Publish home consumption
consumptionEnabled.description: Publish a Matter electrical sensor reporting total house load. Requires consumption CTs installed on the gateway.

consumptionName.title: Home consumption name
consumptionName.description: Name of the consumption sensor. Defaults to "<Name> Home Consumption".

gridEnabled.title: Publish grid flow
gridEnabled.description: Publish a Matter electrical meter reporting what crosses the service entrance — imported from the utility and exported to it. Neither production nor house load answers this on its own, because solar consumed on site never touches the grid, so without this sensor a controller cannot work out grid use.

gridName.title: Grid name
gridName.description: Name of the grid sensor. Defaults to "<Name> Grid".

gridSplit.title: Publish grid as two sensors
gridSplit.description: Publish grid import and grid export as two separate one-directional sensors instead of one sensor carrying both. A single endpoint declaring both directions is legal Matter and Homebridge writes both without error, but on an iOS 27 beta (August 2026) the Home app showed only the exported half and silently ignored import. Two one-directional endpoints match the shape of the production and consumption sensors, which Home handles correctly. Turning this off restores the single combined sensor.

resetHistory.title: Reset energy history (generation)
resetHistory.description: Increase this number to start the Home app's energy history over. The sensors are republished under new identities, so the Home app treats them as new devices, and cumulative energy is published from zero instead of from the gateway's lifetime total. Use it when a sensor's history is unusable — for example when a newly added sensor recorded its entire lifetime counter as a single hour, which sets the chart axis and makes every real bar beside it unreadable. Leave at 0 to keep publishing the gateway's own lifetime totals. The old sensors and their history stay in the Home app under their previous identity until you remove them there; the new ones start empty and need a day of data before they appear in Electricity Usage.

resetHistoryPerSensor.title: Reset energy history — individual sensors
resetHistoryPerSensor.description: Per-sensor overrides of the reset generation above. Set one to start just that sensor's history over while every other sensor keeps its own. An override replaces the value above for that sensor rather than adding to it.

experimentalSensors.title: Publish experimental test sensors
experimentalSensors.description: Publishes two extra sensors alongside the real ones, purely to observe how the Home app treats an endpoint that declares both energy directions: "<Grid name> Test" (one endpoint carrying both grid directions) and "<Solar name> Test" (a SolarPower endpoint carrying production as export and the house's grid draw as import). Leave this off unless you are running that comparison. The extra sensors report energy the real ones already report, and the solar one's import figure is the home's, not the array's — it is deliberately not true of the device it sits on.

energyDeviceTypes.title: Use Matter energy device types
energyDeviceTypes.description: Publishes production as SolarPower (0x17) and consumption as ElectricalMeter (0x0514) instead of a plain electrical sensor. ElectricalSensor (0x0510) is a *utility* class device type, which per the Matter spec is not meant to stand alone as a device — so a controller may not treat the sensors as separate devices and can add them together on the summary tile. Confirmed working on an iOS 27 beta (August 2026): production appears as its own device in Electricity Usage with its energy counted as exported. Homebridge does not expose these device types officially, so they are read from matter.js directly; falls back to a plain electrical sensor if unavailable. Replaces the earlier solarPowerDeviceType option, which still works.

refreshInterval.title: Refresh interval (seconds)
refreshInterval.description: How often to read the gateway. Live power is pushed every poll; lifetime energy at most once a minute.
